title: Congress Can Do More to Defend U.S. Alliances
gist: Drennan and Tabatabai argue the new Democratic Congress should move beyond rhetoric to defend U.S. alliances by integrating allies into the U.S. defense industrial base (ITAR exemptions, DPA Title III, co-production of Patriot PAC-3 and counter-drone systems, allied shipbuilding), forcing timely approvals, extending troop-floor protections, and curbing Trump's tariff and coercion powers.

insights.claim: Trump's actions have soured commercial defense relationships and pushed allies toward domestic or alternative suppliers even as allied defense spending rises rapidly.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Risk of U.S. defense primes losing allied export share to European/domestic suppliers.
insights.quote: pushed allies toward domestic or alternative suppliers
insights.locator: Amid rapidly increasing allied defense spending

insights.claim: Congress could treat more allies as part of the U.S. defense industrial base: expand the National Technology and Industrial Base, extend AUKUS-style ITAR exemptions beyond Australia and the U.K., designate allies as domestic sources under DPA Title III, and raise congressional-notification thresholds for arms sales to close allies.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Legislation easing ITAR/DPA barriers would expand cross-border defense supply chains and allied contractor access.
insights.locator: First, Congress could treat more allies

insights.claim: Congress should fund co-production of Patriot PAC-3 and other air-defense interceptors and counter-drone capabilities, withholding funds until the Pentagon certifies progress, mirroring an SASC proposal for a second source of Patriot interceptor rocket motors.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Watch for interceptor and solid rocket motor second-sourcing contracts.
insights.quote: the same mechanism that the Senate Armed Services Committee has proposed to ensure access to a second source for Patriot interceptor rocket motors

insights.claim: Allied shipbuilding could supplement the SHIPS for America Act through exemptions to 10 USC 8679; the U.S.-Canada-Finland Icebreaker Collaboration Effort Pact, with Finnish yards building the first new U.S. Coast Guard icebreakers in decades, is a template.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Allied shipyards (Finland, Korea, Japan) could win U.S. naval/coast guard work.
insights.quote: Finnish shipyards are building the first new U.S. Coast Guard icebreakers in decades
insights.locator: Here, the Icebreaker Collaboration Effort Pact

insights.claim: A supplemental appropriation could fund munitions production in the U.S. and allied countries, requiring allies to co-fund each co-production initiative they join.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Potential munitions supplemental is a demand catalyst for munitions makers.

insights.claim: Congress could extend foreign repair exemptions under 10 USC 8680 to South Korea and Japan, as already permitted for U.S. submarines in Australian and U.K. shipyards.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Opens U.S. Navy repair work to Korean and Japanese shipyards.

insights.claim: Open-ended approval requirements give the executive an implicit veto; Hegseth reportedly has not completed paperwork for allies to transfer their own Patriot interceptors to Ukraine.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Administrative delays restrict air-defense flows to Ukraine.

insights.claim: The authors propose automatic approvals if the executive fails to act within a set period and standing consent for transfers among treaty allies.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai

insights.claim: Section 1249 of the 2026 NDAA bars U.S. troop reductions in Europe below 76,000 without certification from the EUCOM commander and defense secretary; the authors want similar floors for South Korea in the 2027 NDAA.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Statutory troop floors reduce tail risk of abrupt U.S. withdrawal from Europe/Korea.
insights.quote: bars U.S. troop reductions in Europe below 76,000

insights.claim: Congress can bind the executive by withholding funds pending certification, setting firm obligation deadlines and authorizing multiyear procurement that is harder for one president to unwind.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Multiyear procurement authorizations give defense contractors revenue visibility.
insights.locator: Congress can make its legislative priorities bite

themes.theme: Curbing tariffs and coercion of allies

insights.claim: After the Supreme Court ruled in February that presidents may impose tariffs only with clear congressional authorization, the administration shifted to a temporary surcharge and then Section 301 tariffs that include allies.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Tariff regime has migrated to Section 301; legal basis remains contestable.
insights.locator: After the Supreme Court confirmed in February

insights.claim: Congress could pass something like the bipartisan Trade Review Act, making any new tariff lapse after 60 days without congressional approval.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Would sharply cap tariff duration risk for importers and allies.
insights.quote: would make any new tariff lapse after 60 days without congressional approval
insights.locator: After the Supreme Court confirmed in February

insights.claim: The authors frame reasserting alliance policy as part of Democrats' affordability agenda, since Trump's tariffs on close allies have added to Americans' woes while allied economic integration can spur growth and jobs.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Affordability politics may drive tariff rollbacks on allies.

insights.claim: Because stand-alone bills and appropriations amendments to rein in Trump have stalled, lawmakers should attach protections (e.g., barring funds for military action or annexation against NATO territory after the Greenland crisis) to must-pass legislation.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Watch NDAA/appropriations riders as the effective vehicle for constraints.

insights.claim: Compliance mechanisms can force the administration's hand but cannot force allies to keep investing in a partner they no longer trust.
insights.speaker: John Drennan, Ariane Tabatabai
insights.so_what: Allied hedging and strategic autonomy spending likely persists regardless of Congress.
